title: Polygon triangulations and flips
notes: Keep one adult at each of the three tables; adults can rule or record a child-chosen filling. On a return visit, K-1 can keep a line while completing a polygon (P4) or change one line (P5-6); P6 needs only the pentagon and can follow P2 directly. Grades 2-3 can use their pentagon gallery for the odd return and the flip map (P4-5), with the hexagon one-flip and shortest-route problems (P3, P6), leaving the full hexagon collection (P7) for a separate investigation. Grades 4-5 can revisit shortest fan routes (P4-5) and then the general fan rule or connectivity (P6-7). Preserve labeled boards, tracings and written routes between visits.

Provide eleven pencils/straightedges for the current 4/4/3 children and about 20 tracing sheets cut into quarters, about ten quarters for each of the seven older children (page 2). Since the November 6, 2026 kid-fit revision (F14-*-v5), K-1 draws on large printed boards with no tracing paper, and the older bands write routes as lists of flips.
